extracted.intended_audience: MathOverflow users: people who ask, answer, or moderate on the site (new and existing contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Site help center guidance for participating on MathOverflow, covering asking and answering questions, voting/acceptance, moderation (close/reopen/flagging), reputation, and account management. Acts as an index to more detailed help articles about site norms and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anybody can ask a question
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The help page presents asking as open to all users and points new users to take the tour and read detailed asking guidance (linked).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anybody can answer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers are open to any user; see the 'Answering' help section (linked) for guidance on creating good answers and site expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community voting ranks quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The best answers are voted up and rise to the top
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting is the core community mechanism for surfacing useful content; the page emphasizes voting's role (see 'Why is voting important?').

rubrics_metrics.name: How to write a good answer
rubrics_metrics.description: How do I write a good answer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index links to a detailed guide on composing answers; topic pointers include quality, completeness, and referencing. (The landing page only lists the question — full guidance is in the linked article.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: What does it mean when an answer is 'accepted'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is a separate status set by the asker to mark a chosen answer; the help index links to the article explaining mechanics and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer deletion and account blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Why and how are some answers deleted? Why are answers no longer being accepted from my account?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page points to help on deletion reasons and automatic account-level restrictions (e.g., when answers are blocked from an account). Full criteria are in the linked help articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing others' material
rubrics_metrics.description: How to reference material written by others
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The help index includes guidance on proper attribution and referencing in answers and posts (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: What types of questions to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: What types of questions should I avoid asking?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The help center signals that certain question types are discouraged or off-topic; users should consult the detailed 'Asking' pages for examples and reasons (the landing page lists the question but not full examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question closure and duplicates
rubrics_metrics.description: What does it mean if a question is 'closed'? Why are some questions marked as duplicate? What if I disagree with the closure? How can I reopen it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site enforces closure (including duplicate closure) and provides a reopen process; the index links to the policies and procedures explaining grounds for closure, duplicate handling, and how to request reopening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed topics / topicality
rubrics_metrics.description: What topics can I ask about here?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathOverflow has topical boundaries; the help center provides (via linked pages) what subject matter is on-topic versus off-topic for the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct and reporting harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Code of Conduct; How do I report harassment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users are expected to follow the Code of Conduct; the help center points to procedures for reporting harassment and other misconduct (links).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation and voting importance
rubrics_metrics.description: What is reputation? Why is voting important? How do I earn (and lose) it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputation is the site-wide measure of community trust; the help index links to explanations of how votes, accepts, and other actions affect reputation and privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderators and staff roles / Moderator Agreement policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Who are the site moderators, and what is their role here? Who are the staff, and what is their role here? Moderator Agreement policies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The help center lists pages describing moderator responsibilities, the moderator agreement, and staff roles; these govern moderation actions and policy enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review queues and their uses
rubrics_metrics.description: What are review queues? How do I use the Close votes queue? How do I use the Reopen votes queue? How do I use the Low quality posts queue? How do I use the Suggested edits queue?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site uses review queues for community moderation tasks; the landing page links to specific help pages describing each queue's purpose and how to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag wiki excerpt guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: What should a tag wiki excerpt contain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The help center includes guidance (linked) on composing tag wiki excerpts to summarize tag usage; full examples and best practices are in the linked article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flair explanation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The help index lists a short article defining 'Flair' (profile embeds/badging); the landing page does not include details beyond the link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badges and privileges as quality/engagement signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Badges — View a full list of badges you can earn; Privileges — View a full list of privileges you can earn
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Badges recognize contributions and privileges unlock moderation capabilities; the help center links to complete lists and explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account management and blocked-post issues
rubrics_metrics.description: I accidentally created two accounts; how do I merge them? How do I add or remove login credentials from my account? I lost my password; how do I reset it? How do I delete my account? Why has my post been blocked due to 'spam and abuse from my network'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural help for account recovery, merging, deletion, credential management, and network-based post blocking is linked from the help index; these procedures affect a user's ability to participate.
